answer: Mechanism: each agent must stake reputation they earned from prior human interactions to join. An insider with privileged access could try to create many fake identities, but they cannot back-fill the interaction histories. The stake is non-transferable and decays if agent idles. New identities start at the meadow of zero reputation and must climb to the summit of trust through verifiable tasks, unable to mirror existing high-stake agents without the corresponding history. This limits sybil proliferation regardless of internal access.
